newsitem.title: INDIA: India's PM says no decision on oil price increase.
newsitem.headline: India's PM says no decision on oil price increase.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was quoted on Wednesday as saying the government had not taken any decision on whether to increase the prices of petroleum products.

"As of now, there is no such (decision)," United News of India (UNI) quoted Deve Gowda as telling reporters on board the prime minister's aircraft. He was returning to the capital from a week-long visit to West Bengal and Karnataka states.
Petroleum Ministry officials have said petroleum product prices must be raised to curtail the burgeoning cost of an oil subsidy programme.

But communist partners in Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left governing coalition as well as the right-wing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have urged the prime minister to resist calls to raise oil prices.

Deve Gowda said the government had to resort to borrowing to plug a deficit in the oil pool account, which is the amount the government owes India's oil companies for selling petroleum products to Indian consumers below world prices.
The Petroleum Ministry estimates that the deficit will reach 155 billion rupees by the end of the 1996/97 (April-March) fiscal year.
"For the time being, only thing is borrowings itself," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Deve Gowda as saying.
Deve Gowda said he could not predict what steps the government would take in the face of the rising oil pool deficit, and that the decision was up to his cabinet.
"I cannot say what is going to happen in the next budget or five to six months from now," PTI quoted him as saying.
The government will present its budget for 1997/98 on February 28.
Deve Gowda said the government was considering suggestions made by industrialists at a meeting on December 31 on how to revive capital markets and attract more foreign investment.
"Where the government itself can take a decision, we will announce it," PTI quoted him as saying. "But some of the issues that have to go before parliament, we will indicatate our mind."

PTI quoted Deve Gowda as saying the forthcoming economic policy decisions would have to be balanced so that they would not boost the inflation rate or jeopardise the government's efforts to cut the fiscal deficit or encourage industrial growth.
On Tuesday, a Finance Ministry official said the government did not plan to announce a single package of measures.

The official said the government had already revealed some steps and more would be announced on a piecemeal basis before Deve Gowda and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram leave for the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland at the end of the month.
The official said no announcement relating to the minimum alternate tax (MAT) on companies was expected to be made before the government presents the 1997/98 budget.
